# NPM Improved v1.2.3

NPM Improved v1.2.3 permanently fixes a lifecycle-updater architecture problem that could cause every future UI update to keep executing an old updater implementation.

## What was happening

The in-app updater correctly replaced the NPM Improved application container, but the helper container launched:

```text
<host-project>/scripts/update-handoff.sh
```

from the original Git checkout on the Docker host.

An in-app image update does not update that checkout.

As a result, an installation could be running a newer NPM Improved UI/backend while still executing the updater script from an older release. That is why newer releases could continue reporting the old generic:

```text
Docker could not pull ghcr.io/gigabytegrove/npm-improved:vX.Y.Z
```

even after newer fallback logic had been added to the application source.

## The permanent fix

The handoff script is now embedded in every NPM Improved runtime image.

When Update, Restart, or Rollback is started, the backend reads the handoff implementation from the **currently running application image** and injects that exact version into the temporary Docker CLI helper.

The host project directory is still mounted so the helper can safely work with:

- Compose files;
- `.env`;
- persistent data;
- the Docker socket.

But the host checkout's `scripts/update-handoff.sh` is no longer executed.

This makes lifecycle behavior versioned with NPM Improved itself.

## Update-source behavior

The embedded handoff retains the dual update path introduced in v1.2.1:

1. try the official GHCR image;
2. if that is unavailable, download the architecture-specific public GitHub Release Docker bundle;
3. verify the bundle against the published SHA-256 checksum;
4. load the verified image into Docker;
5. replace the application container;
6. verify health and build identity;
7. automatically restore the previous image if verification fails.

## CI proof

Docker CI now deliberately removes the host checkout's `scripts/update-handoff.sh` before exercising the native lifecycle manager.

The Restart operation must still complete successfully.

Updater capabilities also report:

```text
handoff_source: embedded
embedded_handoff_available: true
```

and lifecycle controls are disabled if a runtime image is ever built without its embedded handoff.

## One-time bridge from older releases

v1.2.2 and earlier still launch the updater from the host checkout because that behavior is part of those already-installed versions.

A one-time bridge to v1.2.3 may therefore be required on an affected installation.

After v1.2.3 is running, future lifecycle updates use the embedded implementation and no longer depend on keeping the host Git checkout synchronized with the application image.
